claims.claim: The platform team's decision that sync impersonation ships behind a per-project flag, with rollout gated project-by-project until the diff story is fixed, directly contradicts RFC-001's stated Goal that 'the feature can be enabled/disabled only at the system level. Once enabled/disabled, it is applicable to all Argo CD Applications' — the RFC's system-wide toggle has no per-project granularity, so implementing the note's decision requires re-opening an approved RFC goal (approvers @alexmt/@crenshaw-dev/@jannfis) rather than just flipping a flag.

strategy.md commits that 'deletion of generated Applications is explicitly out of scope for rollout orchestration: ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children will not be implemented,' while prd-progressive-sync-deletion.md is a shipped proposal that adds exactly that: a `deletionOrder` field (AllAtOnce/Reverse) giving ApplicationSets ordered, automated child-deletion. One of these two owning documents (roadmap vs. PRD author @ranakan19) is stale and needs to be reconciled before either can be treated as the current commitment.

T-28927's maturity-review scope call freezes 'strategy.rollingSync.steps (the matchExpressions list, one match-set per step)' as the backward-compatibility-bound v1 shape once Progressive Sync ships Stable, requiring any change to how a step is expressed to land as a new field rather than an in-place restructuring — but T-28755's proposed API sketch nests a `parallel` list of matchExpressions directly inside `rollingSync.steps` entries, restructuring the frozen step shape in place instead of introducing it as a separate field. Whoever owns the Stable-promotion scope call needs to force T-28755 into a new-field shape (e.g. a sibling `parallelGroups`) before it can land post-freeze.
